pr_title: tikv: support cancel before cop response return
pr_body: ### What problem does this PR solve? Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/18057 continue to https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/18277 Problem Summary: now cop task maybe cannot exit due to goroutine blocked in grpc and could not see kill flag ### What is changed and how it works? What's Changed, How it Works: we cannot cancel root context, but we can cancel "context used to send rpc" so this PR chooses to collect CancelFunc for each RPCs in a cop query and cancel them during executor closing. ### Related changes - n/a ### Check List Tests - Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below) ``` 1. start a cluster with pd and tikv(need inject in batchclient which need tikv instead of mocktikv or unistore) 2. start two mysql sessions: A and B 3. `curl -XPUT -d 'return(true)' http://0.0.0.0:10080/fail/github.com/pingcap/tidb/store/tikv/mockBlockOnBatchClient` to enable failpoint which cause every kv request will block 1 hour 4. execute a cop SQL like `select * from t` it will blocked in session A 5. `show processlist` and `kill tidb query N` in session B ``` - without 40b7b26 will see query cannot be kill and goroutine blocked in ticlient and recvFromRespCh - without other's will see goroutine block in ticlient and copIterator.Close - with this pr will see query can be killed and report error Side effects - n/a ### Release note - support cancel before RPC response return. --- This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/pingcap/tidb/18445)

issue_context.title: executor: avoid goroutine leak in TableReader along with memory leak
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->
The [source code](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/ddcc89dc793fbc89852071702996ea212c342efb/store/tikv/coprocessor.go#L529) only generates go routines, but not handle errors if some exceptions happens.
To to reproduce this issue using failpoint.

On the other hand, if the main thread is cancelled, those generated goroutines should stop correctly.

detail problems:

- [ ] TableReader->Next() is blocked, how to stop the execution once cancel the query manually?
- [ ] When call TableReader->Close(), how to stop coprocessor workers?
- [ ] When coprocessor workes panic, how to cancel the query correctly?
- [ ] what about IndexReader?


### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
all goroutine stops and return errors.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
other goroutine runs normally and occupy many memory .

### 4. Affected version (Required)
v4.0.x, v3
<!-- v3.0.0, v4.0.0, etc -->

### 5. Root Cause Analysis
lack handing exceptions.

<!-- should be filled by the investigator before it's closed -->
comments:
Good questions, I'm glad to answer them:

1. TableReader->Next() is blocked, how to stop the execution once cancel the query manually?

Everytime executor.Next is called, the `killed` flag is checked.
If the code is blocked within `TableReader->Next()` and never run to the Next() function, we should check why it's blocked and check the flag there.

For example, we have already check the [pessimistic lock waiting](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/12852), each [backoff](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/14552) and [coprocessor finish one region](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/15615).

 2. When call TableReader->Close(), how to stop coprocessor workers?

The correct order should be coprocessor throw an error (maybe ErrInterrupted) to TableReader, then TableReader call Close() function.

We should not let TableReader peceive kill during the coprocessor worker is working, exception handling is hard that way. 
Instead, only one place handle the `kill` flag and turn it into ErrInterrupted. 
Exception handling is turned into error handling which is much easier.

3. When coprocessor workes panic, how to cancel the query correctly?

When the coprocessor workes panic, it should throw error to the caller -- TableReader, then the TableReader handle the error.

4. what about IndexReader?

The same with TableReader.

It's important to understand that there is no real `cancel` operation.
It's wrong to think like a caller preceive the `killed` flag and cancel the worker.
killed flag is checked  only when some code runs to check it, in this way exception handling is turned to error handling.

review_comments: Is it necessary to use `map`? because it seems here just one cancel function.

one CopIterator will fork many CopWorkers and parallel send CopTasks, so rpcCancel will catch more than one CancelFunc, and at last, we need use map instead of slice to make remove itself easier when cancel be called
I think only a cancel function in copIterator is ok, becase copIteratorWorker can share the cancel to stop work.
Does the `id` work here? because it is just a temporary variable at L:298
the `id` will be caught by the cancel closure and help remove cancel from map, it just help avoid memory leak for after cancel be executed
Why need to delete here? The `cancel` function can be repeated call, so the `delete` here is redundant?
should cancel be invoked every case?
we can do it, but it always be noop function when `retry == true` or `err != nil`
should this cancel() be called here?

yes, the trick in here is `RPCCancellerCtxKey{}` only will be attached when it's a non-streaming request, for non-streaming request, the response will be exhausted before this function return，so it's safe to call it at here.
if it needs retry, is this `cancel()` necessary?
it's a practice to call cancel() when WithCancel context never be used, and this also help remove memory in `cancels` map
If RPCCanceller has been cancelled, do we need to send request to tiflash ?

If RPCCanceller has been cancelled, sendRequest will immediately be returned， but it may send a request for 50% probability due to go's `select case` for multiple available channels.

emmm..we can check ctx.Done before sending for every request but check the channel is cost-operator, maybe better avoid this handle for this extreme case- -？
